jobs.title: Managing Director, Marketing & Communications
jobs.description:
Application Instructions

Click Apply to submit your online application. Please attach a resume and thoughtful cover letter on the "My Experience" page in the "Resume/CV" field.

Active City Year Staff members must login to Workday to apply internally.

Number of Positions: 1

Compensation: $115,000.00 - $120,000.00 Annually Commensurate with Experience and Location

Work Location: Temporarily Hybrid On-Site/Remote

Position Overview

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Managing Director of Marketing & Communications (MarCom) is a strategic leader who proactively creates and elevates our messaging and communication strategy to raise awareness of our mission, expand our media presence, and deepen connection among key stakeholders. The Managing Director of MarCom will oversee and support the implementation of City Year’s branding strategy in Los Angles to ensure consistent coherent representation of CYLA’s impact across all departments and communication outlets, including CYLA’s social media platforms. As a member of the City Year Los Angeles Senior Leadership Team (SLT), they will be a highly effective storyteller who can bring to life City Year’s impact. They will manage the Sr. Marketing & Communications Manager.

This position is perfect for someone who is entrepreneurial with proven communications experience, and who is a proactive leader, creative, strategic thinker, and willing to challenge old conventions to push beyond traditional communications.

The ideal candidate cares deeply about addressing systemic inequities in education and can represent CYLA powerfully in community spaces. This individual should be able to operate at a high level, able to think about the big picture and the best way to communicate and engage the community at large.

City Year values and continuously works to build an equitable and inclusive culture where people with diverse lived experiences feel they belong.

Responsibilities

Job Description

Marketing & Communications Strategy

In partnership with the Executive Director, Board Members, SLT, and the City Year headquarters’ teams, lead the development and implementation of a strategic and diversified Marketing & Communications plan that meets current goals and anticipates future needs and growth objectives.
Lead 20th Anniversary Board Committee to create and implement milestone Marketing & Communication strategy.
Develop clear communication cascade and strategy for disseminating communications to external audiences (e.g., communication medium, audience, etc.)
Leverage and amplify the national organizational Marketing, Communications, and Creative teams’ content, strategy, and materials to advance the Los Angeles and organizational impact.
In collaboration with the Managing Director of Development, create the strategy, messaging, and design of all fundraising communications, including event invitations, sponsorship decks, event programs, donor-facing videos, and stage remarks.
In collaboration with the Impact team, analyze ongoing program data to support storytelling of the impact of our work throughout the year.
Develop and implement strategic initiatives aimed at building awareness of CYLA locally by leveraging LA assets that strengthen the brand.
Collaborate with Managing Director of Government Relations to position City Year in the community and with public officials to help build awareness of our work and garner support.
Deepen City Year Los Angeles’ presence and reputation in communities where we serve.

Senior Leadership & Staff Management

As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, develop Los Angeles site strategic plan and lead implementing the site’s local operating plan.
Work with SLT and national leaders to understand priorities and business goals and develop strategies to meet the organization’s needs.
Serve as a strategic advisor to SLT on narrative positioning, reputational considerations, and public-facing communications including major fundraising moments and campaigns.
Leverage Board where appropriate to reach departmental and site-wide marketing & communication goals.
Serve as a CYLA representative at local events and community functions.
Manage the Sr. Marketing & Communications Manager, building and maintaining a relationship by creating an environment of open and honest two-way communication.
Provide both positive and constructive feedback and coaching to support direct report’s development.
Ensure professional accountability with direct report and team through clear expectations, weekly check-ins, and formal performance reviews.
Partner with all City Year Los Angeles departments through site events, projects, and cross-departmental committees as needed to ensure site-wide goals are met.

Marketing Implementation

Oversee the development of clear and consistent CYLA branding and messaging for external stakeholders, in line with org-wide parameters.
In collaboration with the Sr. Marketing and Communications Manager and a contracted designer, oversee all marketing and branding materials to be used regularly at CYLA events, recruiting efforts, and external communications.
In collaboration with the Development team, develop a multi-tiered email drip campaign for new donors, top-of-funnel volunteers, and general stakeholders, guiding them through a tailored engagement journey with clear communications and desired outcomes based on audience segmentation.
Support content development for City Year Los Angeles’ Instagram, Facebook and Twitter accounts, blog, E-newsletter, eBlasts, and publication of all other electronic communications.
Ensure consistency of messaging within CYLA by sharing expectations, tone, and content with other departments.

Content Strategy & Storytelling

Oversee creation of all communications collateral, including multi-media, videos, website, media materials, and other items as needed.
Oversee the creation of annual impact reports tailored for individual donors, foundations, program sponsors, and team sponsors to ensure meaningful stewardship and donor recognition.
Support development and core messaging for all major fundraising initiatives, including the annual Spring Break Gala, ensuring alignment across all communications, collateral, and event deliverables.
Collaborate on language for donor proposals and work with the grants consultant to develop and annually renew a compelling, cohesive case for support.
Oversee the training and development of corps members to effectively share their story through leadership roles such as Communication Corps, Yellow Jacket Society Ambassadors, and CE Ambassadors.
In collaboration with the Managing Director of People & Operations support effective internal communications processes across the site.

Media Relations

In partnership with Actum, support overall public relations strategy for CYLA, as well as for specific strategic campaigns and initiatives.
Oversee Sr. Manager of Communications in the development of media strategies for City Year Los Angeles’ marquee events, including Spring Break, Opening Day, Martin Luther King, Jr. Day of Service, and other Service Days as needed throughout the year.
Develop and oversee messaging calendar to be commensurate with City Year benchmarks and milestones throughout the year, including national events, media pitches, and external partnerships.
Seeks external opportunities to showcase key executives in public forums including panel participation and keynote speaking opportunities.
Secure high-impact coverage that elevates CYLA programs and advocacy efforts while reinforcing brand leadership.
Manage relationships with media outlets, journalists, and external PR partners.
Support Executive Director and SLT with preparation, messaging, and follow-up for media appearances and public engagements.

Key Competencies:

In order to succeed in this role, an applicant must have the following competencies:

Strategic Thinking: Collaborates cross-functionally to develop and translate strategies into action plans that build the capacity of the site/department. Focuses the organization/department and resources on efforts that add significant strategic value.
Communication: Ability to communicate to diverse audiences using compelling storytelling; clearly articulates information and ideas. Inspires and connects with diverse audiences through both written and verbal communication. Listens carefully and responds thoughtfully to feedback.
Collaboration: Creates and sustains mutually beneficial, long-term and transformational partnerships for City Year with communities and organizations. Strategically and consistently cultivates new and existing partnerships with stakeholders with aligned and different interests.
Decision Making: Drives organizational decision-making processes to produce timely decisions that include the right people, data, and context. Anticipates impact of decisions/ actions on multiple stakeholders across the organization and outside of organization. Plans for how decisions will be communicated and executed to build alignment and investment.
Learning: City Year has a unique service model and organizational culture. Successful applicants will have strong experience and a proven track record of success in the above areas, but must also be willing and eager to continue to learn.

Minimum Qualifications

An accomplished leader with 8-10+ years of proven success in external relations, marketing, or media leadership; nonprofit or mission-driven experience preferred.
At least 3 years of management experience with strong track record of results:
Setting high expectations and holding self and team accountable for performance goals
Developing diverse talent through performance plans, reviews and leadership opportunities
Using progress and outcome data to inform team management.

Strong digital fluency, including CMS platforms, email marketing tools, analytics, and social media platforms.
Authorized documentation to work in the United States of America
Criminal background history clearance to work with school-age children, depending on the position

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of the Los Angeles community & educational organizations.
Committed to City Year’s mission of partnering with public schools in systemically under-resourced communities to prepare students with the skills and mindsets they need to thrive in school and in life
Flexibility to meet sudden and unpredictable partnership needs and willingness to work outside standard established business hours.
City Year/AmeriCorps experience is a plus.
Bachelor's degree in communications or similar preferred.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to sit, stand, and walk around for extended periods.
Move about the office or event location as needed throughout the workday.
Manual dexterity for typing, writing, and handling office equipment
Visual acuity to read screens and printed materials.
Hearing ability to participate in conversations and respond to phone calls.
Ability to communicate clearly in person, by phone, and in writing.

Working Conditions:

Based in LA with an average 3-4 in-person days per week.
Regular travel across LA. Locations vary based on events or projects.
Flexible schedule and location based on role responsibilities.
Typical schedule: 40 hours per week with occasional extended hours as needed.
Some afterhours and weekend work.
Noise levels are generally moderate.
Must have reliable internet access for remote or flexible work arrangements.

Benefits

Full-time employees will be eligible for all benefits including vacation, sick days and organization holidays. You may participate in all benefit programs that City Year establishes and makes available to eligible employees, under (and subject to all provisions of) the plan documents that govern those programs. jobs.title: Chief Program Officer
jobs.description:
Athena is a New York State Office of Mental Health-licensed provider serving more than 8,000 individuals across our Upstate and Downstate clinics. We are seeking a Chief Program Officer to provide strategic and clinical leadership across our existing service lines while driving the thoughtful expansion of programs to address evolving community needs and increase access to high-quality behavioral healthcare.

The Chief Program Officer (CPO) is Athena’s senior clinical and programmatic executive responsible for the quality, effectiveness, consistency, and continued development of the organization’s clinical programs and services across New York State. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the CPO ensures that Athena’s continued growth is supported by strong clinical infrastructure, evidence-based practice, regulatory compliance, measurable outcomes, and exceptional patient care.

The CPO provides executive oversight of clinical leadership, program performance, quality improvement, workforce development, and new program implementation, working closely with the CEO, COO, CMO, and other organizational leaders.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Provide executive oversight of Athena’s clinical quality, clinical leaders, and standards of care across locations and service lines to support consistency in treatment outcomes
Establish consistent, evidence-based, patient-centered, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive clinical practices
Ensure appropriate systems for clinical supervision, high-risk case review, treatment planning, care coordination, and continuity of care
Develop and mentor clinical and program leaders while promoting accountability, collaboration, and professional excellence
Establish and monitor clinical quality, outcomes, access, engagement, retention, and program performance metrics
Use clinical data to proactively identify risks, trends, and opportunities for improvement
Ensure adherence to OMH and other applicable regulatory and clinical requirements
Lead clinical quality-improvement initiatives and support regulatory reviews, audits, and corrective action activities
Provide clinical leadership for the development, implementation, and stabilization of new programs, locations, and models of care
Evaluate opportunities for program expansion based on community need, outcomes, organizational strategy, and clinical feasibility
Lead the executive team in aligning clinical strategy with organizational growth, operations, workforce planning, and financial sustainability
Represent Athena’s clinical programs and capabilities with regulators, health systems, payers, community organizations, and other external stakeholders

Key Performance Areas: Success in this role will be measured through demonstrated improvement and sustained performance in areas including

Patient access and timely engagement in care
Clinical quality and patient outcomes
Patient retention and continuity of care
High-risk patient management and clinical safety
Clinical documentation and regulatory compliance
Clinician productivity, retention, and engagement
Clinical supervision and leadership effectiveness
Successful implementation and stabilization of new programs
Patient and referral-partner experience
Consistency of clinical standards across programs and locations
Ensuring financial stability of behavioral health programs

Qualifications:

Master’s degree or doctorate in social work, psychology, counseling, mental health counseling, or another relevant behavioral health discipline required
Active New York State clinical licensure strongly preferred; independent clinical licensure such as LCSW, LMHC, or psychologist preferred
Minimum of 8 years of progressive behavioral health leadership experience, including significant responsibility for clinical programs, quality, and staff leadership
Demonstrated experience overseeing multi-site and/or large-scale outpatient behavioral health services. Strong knowledge of New York State behavioral health regulations and OMH-licensed services strongly preferred
Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and scaling clinical programs. Strong understanding of evidence-based treatment, clinical risk management, quality improvement, measurement-based care, and behavioral health outcomes
Experience leading senior clinical leaders and multidisciplinary teams
Demonstrated ability to use clinical and operational data to identify trends, improve performance, and drive organizational decision-making
Exceptional communication, leadership, collaboration, and change-management skills

Working Conditions

This position will be located at one of Athena’s licensed clinic locations, with the ability to travel between offices as needed. This is a professional work environment where a computer, desk, chair and office supplies will be provided onsite at each of our offices.

Physical Requirements:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee in order to successfully perform the essential functions of the role above.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to hear and speak on the phone or computer throughout the day, stand and sit for an extended period of time and be able to write and answer emails in addition to carrying objects no greater than 25 pounds, when needed.

Make banking a Fifth Third better®

We connect great people to great opportunities. Are you ready to take the next step? Discover a career in banking at Fifth Third Bank.

OUR RESPONSIBILITIES:

The responsibilities for this role are below; you may support projects of varying complexity based on skill and organizational priorities.   

Responsible for growing and retaining relationships with targeted client group by coordinating all aspects of the client relationship through the delivery of value-added financial solutions (ranging from traditional to customized products) to existing and prospective clients that will help them to enhance their business.
Develops business development strategy to generate new business.
Provides leadership and direction to other credit staff and fosters strong communication between customers and internal staff from application through closing.
Coordinates all client-facing activities related to their clients, including credit support and other product area (e.g., Treasury Management) partners.
Responsible for the review and underwriting of credit requests and insuring appropriateness and satisfaction level of existing services provided.
Responsible for developing revenue growth through generation of loans, deposits, fee income and cross selling all applicable bank services to existing customer base, and to identify and solicit bank services to non-customers.

Develops intimate knowledge of all customers and prospect opportunities.

Responsible for relationship review and overall relationship profitability.
Works with Portfolio Manager, Credit Analysts, and other members of the Credit Department to underwrite credit requests.

Visibility to leadership as mentor in training, retention and development of talent. 
High attention to detail and commitment to deliver high quality work product consistently. 
Strong project management skills and ability to manage a team. 
Strong collaboration, communication and leadership skills. 
Ability to obtain and maintain required securities licenses in accordance with company policy. 

SKILLS FOR SUCCESS:

Successful candidates will demonstrate a higher degree of proficiency (typically from 8+ years of practical experience or advanced academic exposure) across the following areas:  

Client Advisory & Relationship Management – Ability to lead strategic conversations, build trust, and deliver tailored solutions that deepen client relationships.  
Origination & Commercial Impact – Skilled in identifying opportunities, developing pitches, and converting ideas into revenue-generating engagements.  
Team Leadership & Development – Proven ability to mentor, develop, and lead high-performing teams.  
Market Insight & Thought Leadership – Ability to translate market trends into strategic content and client engagement strategies.  

DOING THE RIGHT THING:
Our employees take pride in doing the right thing for customers and colleagues as well as being accountable for risk by openly exchanging ideas and opinions, elevating concerns, and following policies and procedures that protect all our valuable assets —including you.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
About Roadly 

Roadly is a fast-growing freight brokerage built around exceptional service, disciplined operations, and a strong culture of accountability. As we continue to scale, we're looking for an experienced operations leader to build structure, develop our team, and ensure our operations department continues performing at a high level as the business grows. 

This is not a "keep the lights on" management role. We're looking for someone who can build systems, coach people, improve processes, solve problems before they become problems, and create an operations department capable of supporting the company's next phase of growth. 

Position Summary 

The Director of Operations will lead Roadly's entire Operations Department, including Operations Representatives, Operations Customer Success Managers, and the Carrier Safety & Compliance function. 

This individual will own the day-to-day execution of operations while continuously improving efficiency, accountability, communication, and overall department performance. They will work closely with Sales and Leadership to ensure customers receive exceptional service while building scalable operating processes that support long-term growth. 

Responsibilities 

Team Leadership  

•Lead, coach, and develop the operations department. 
•Establish clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
•Conduct regular one-on-one meetings and performance reviews. 
•Recruit, interview, hire, onboard, and develop operations team members.
•Manage employee performance, corrective action, and terminations when necessary.
•Build a culture centered around accountability, teamwork, urgency, and customer service. 

Operational Excellence 

•Oversee daily freight operations across all customer accounts. 
•Ensure freight moves efficiently while maintaining exceptional customer service.
•Identify operational bottlenecks and implement long-term solutions.
•Standardize processes and continuously improve workflows. 
•Build scalable operating procedures that allow the company to grow efficiently.
•Monitor department KPIs and proactively address performance trends. 

Customer & Sales Alignment 

•Serve as the operational liaison between Sales and Operations. 
•Improve communication during customer onboarding and account transitions. 
•Ensure customer expectations are communicated and executed consistently. 
•Partner with Sales Leadership to solve customer challenges and identify operational opportunities. 

Capacity & Network Management 

•Monitor carrier capacity across key markets and lanes.
•Identify market trends and operational risks before they impact customers.
•Assist with strategic carrier development initiatives. 
•Work closely with the Carrier Safety & Compliance Manager to maintain a high-quality carrier network. 

Safety & Compliance Oversight 

•Provide leadership and support to the Carrier Safety & Compliance Manager.
•Ensure Roadly's Carrier Vetting SOP is consistently followed.
•Review operational trends, audits, and compliance reporting.
•Support continuous improvement of carrier risk management processes. 

Leadership 

•Participate in Leadership Team meetings. 
•Present Operations KPIs, initiatives, challenges, and improvement plans. 
•Collaborate with Leadership on strategic initiatives. 
•Help establish annual operational goals and departmental priorities. 
•Drive a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence throughout 
the organization. 

Qualifications 

Required 

•5+ years of freight brokerage operations experience. 
•Previous experience leading brokerage operations teams. 
•Demonstrated success building systems and improving operational efficiency.
•Strong leadership, coaching, and people development skills.
•Strong knowledge of carrier procurement and capacity management. 
•Experience using transportation management systems (TMS). 
•Familiarity with Highway, Descartes, DAT, Truckstop, and other brokerage technologies.   
•Excellent communication and conflict resolution abilities.
•Comfortable making difficult personnel decisions when necessary. 
•Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail.
•Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 
•Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment
•High sense of ownership, urgency, and accountability. 

Preferred 

•Experience leading teams of 10+ employees.
•Experience developing SOPs, KPIs, and operational reporting. 
•Understanding of carrier compliance, safety, and transportation regulations. 

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12 months, this individual will: 
•Build a highly accountable operations department with clear organizational structure.
•Improve communication and collaboration between Sales and Operations.
•Increase operational efficiency through process improvements and standardization. 
•Develop future leaders within the operations department.
•Implement measurable KPIs and reporting dashboards.
•Strengthen consistency in customer service execution. 
•Position Roadly's operations department to successfully support the company's continued growth. 

Compensation & Benefits 

•Competitive base salary 
•Health benefits 
•Paid time off 
•401(k) 
•Professional development opportunities 

Why Roadly? 

Roadly is in an exciting stage of growth. We're building a company known for operational excellence, exceptional customer service, and a team-first culture. This is an opportunity to have a direct impact on the future of the business by building the operational foundation that supports our next phase of growth. 

If you're a leader who enjoys developing people, improving processes, solving complex operational challenges, and building scalable organizations, we'd love to meet you.

jobs.description:
Company Description
Community Heart & Soul® is a nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening small cities and towns across the United States by fostering healthier, more economically vibrant communities. The organization promotes the Community Heart & Soul model, a resident-driven approach that helps communities identify their values and priorities for long-term success. Community Heart & Soul trains and supports a nationwide network of Certified Community Heart & Soul Coaches who guide local communities through this model. Team members collaborate closely with local leaders, residents, and coaches to expand the reach and impact of community-driven change. The organization offers a mission-driven work environment focused on equity, inclusion, and sustainable community development.

Role Description
Based in Shelburne, Vermont, Community Heart & Soul is seeking a Chief Operating Officer (COO) to serve as the organization's senior internal operating executive. Reporting directly to
the President, the COO leads day-to-day operations, staff coordination, financial management
support, and organizational infrastructure—enabling the President to remain fully focused on
national expansion, partnership development, and strategic growth.

This is a significant leadership opportunity at a compelling moment. Community foundations,
statewide philanthropic networks, and civic organizations are key in the growth of Community
Heart & Soul's resident-led program. The COO will play a central role in ensuring that this
national growth is matched by strong systems, disciplined execution, and a thriving internal
culture—without veering into mission-creep. The COO upholds the organization's commitment
to its core identity as it scales.

This is an in-office position based in Shelburne, VT. Some travel is required to meet with
partners, Heart & Soul communities, and attend conferences and events. 

1. Organizational Operations The COO ensures that Community Heart & Soul runs smoothly, efficiently, and professionally every day. • Oversee day-to-day operations and translate approved strategic priorities into clear, actionable work plans. • Coordinate internal systems across all departments and monitor progress against projects and deadlines. • Identify opportunities to improve workflows, meeting rhythms, reporting systems, and decision-making processes. • Ensure staff have the tools, information, and support needed to do their best work. • Maintain operational momentum and continuity as the organization grows—especially when the President is traveling or externally engaged.

2. Staff Leadership and Culture The COO strengthens accountability while preserving Community Heart & Soul's collaborative culture and mission-centered spirit. • Provide day-to-day management that supports staff and sustains a healthy, highperforming team environment. • Coach managers and staff through operational challenges; support performance management and professional development. • Foster collaboration across the program, communications, market development, finance, and administrative functions. • Preserve the current spirit of trust, flexibility, and shared mission as the organization evolves.

3. Financial and Business Operations Working closely with the Finance Director and President, the COO ensures strong financial management, budget discipline, and businesslike operating practices. • Lead annual budgeting and ongoing budget monitoring in partnership with the Finance Director and President . • Translate budget decisions into operating plans; review operational expenses and identify efficiencies. • Support the Finance Director in preparing the annual audit. • Manage contracts, MOUs, vendor relationships, and purchasing processes. • Ensure financial information is consistently available to inform planning and decisionmaking.

4. Risk Management and Compliance The COO ensures the organization minimizes its risk exposure and protects its assets. • Oversee risk management across contracts, human resources, intellectual property, and organizational compliance. • Ensure that personnel policies are current, clearly communicated, and consistently applied. • Oversee benefits administration, HR compliance, and accurate administrative recordkeeping. • Ensure the organization renews and enforces its trademark protection, domain names (URLs), and other brand-related assets. • Support policy updates and compliance matters that protect the organization's legal standing and reputation.

5. Human Resources and Administration The COO oversees the administrative systems that support staff performance, organizational health, and long-term staffing capacity. • Lead hiring, onboarding, and staff transitions; coordinate performance review processes. • Support staff development and internal communication to build a strong, capable team. • Help ensure the organization is appropriately staffed for current and future needs.

6. Technology and Internal Systems The COO ensures Community Heart & Soul has reliable, scalable systems to support a growing national organization. • Oversee internal technology systems and vendor relationships, including database, CRM, file management, and knowledge management platforms. • Support cybersecurity, data integrity, and technology planning. • Help the organization use technology to improve efficiency, accountability, and partner follow-through.

7. Partnership and Growth Support The COO ensures that the organization's national growth is operationally supported and sustainably managed. • Ensure partnership commitments are tracked, fulfilled, and supported by strong internal systems including MOU’s and Seed Grant tracking. • Coordinate internal readiness for conferences, partner gatherings, and national presentations. • Build scalable systems that allow the organization to grow without outpacing internal capacity. • Help ensure that expanding visibility and demand are met with operational excellence. 8. Board and Governance Support The COO supports the President in preparing for Board meetings, committee work, and governance-related follow-through. • Support preparation of Board materials and track follow-up from Board and leadership meetings. • Help ensure organizational reports are timely, accurate, and useful for governance. • Support governance calendars, annual planning, and policy updates.

About Colorado Mountain Club

Colorado Mountain Club (CMC) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting adventure, recreation, conservation, and education in the outdoors. Founded in 1912, CMC provides access to year-round activities, events, and schools tailored to a wide range of outdoor enthusiasts, from novices to experts. With over 6,000 members, CMC facilitates more than 3,000 trips annually and offers 250+ courses, fostering a dynamic community of adventure seekers and conservationists.

Position Overview

Colorado Mountain Club is seeking a Development Director to lead the next phase of growth and evolution of our fundraising program. This position represents an opportunity to build the foundation for long-term philanthropic success by strengthening donor relationships, improving development systems, and creating a clear pathway for members and supporters to become increasingly engaged with CMC.
The Development Director will serve as the organization's fundraising leader, responsible for developing and executing strategies that increase annual giving, expand major donor relationships, strengthen institutional partnerships, and position CMC for future campaign and legacy giving opportunities. This role is not simply focused on hitting annual revenue targets. It is focused on building a stronger culture of engagement and philanthropy among the thousands of individuals who already connect with CMC through membership, recreation, education, volunteerism, and conservation.

The successful candidate will help transform CMC's development efforts from a transactional fundraising approach into a relationship-based advancement model, creating systems and strategies that move individuals along a lifelong journey from public audience, to CMC member, donor, loyal supporter, and major or legacy donor. The Development Director will report directly to the CEO, serve as a member of the senior leadership team, and work closely with the Board of Directors and Development Committee. Over time, this role may evolve into broader advancement leadership as CMC continues to align development, membership, communications, and community engagement efforts.

Key Competencies

Development Strategy & Fundraising Leadership
Execute a multi-year fundraising strategy aligned with CMC's organizational priorities around donor retention and progression.
Build and manage a comprehensive fundraising program spanning individual annual giving, major gifts, planned giving, foundation support, corporate partnerships, and event engagement.
Establish clear fundraising systems, processes, and performance metrics to support sustainable growth.
Create strategies to increase donor retention, second gifts, recurring giving, and long-term donor loyalty.
Partner with the CEO, Board members, and staff leadership on donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies.

Development Operations & Infrastructure
Strengthen development systems, policies, and processes to support effective fundraising operations.
Manage and improve data quality, reporting, and relationship management practices within Salesforce and other development systems.
Establish consistent practices for gift tracking, donor communications, stewardship, and reporting.
Partner with finance and operations staff to ensure accurate gift processing, reporting, reconciliation, and accountability.
Create dashboards, reports, and internal tools that help leadership understand fundraising performance and donor pipeline progress.

Donor Engagement & Relationship Building
Build authentic relationships with members, volunteers, donors, foundation program officers, corporate partners, and community supporters.
Manage a donor pipeline through research, identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Create meaningful engagement opportunities including donor cultivation events, outdoor experiences, stewardship activities, and personalized outreach.
Serve as a visible ambassador for CMC within Colorado's outdoor community and philanthropic landscape.
Develop personalized donor strategies that strengthen connection to CMC's mission, programs, conservation work, education, and community impact.

Community Engagement & Organizational Collaboration
Work collaboratively with membership and communications staff to create a unified approach to member engagement and donor development.
Help build an integrated community engagement strategy that strengthens the connection between participation, belonging, and philanthropy.
Collaborate on communications, campaigns, events, and storytelling that demonstrate CMC's impact and inspire support.
Support the continued evolution toward an integrated Community Engagement and Advancement model.
Partner across departments to identify donor stories, program outcomes, volunteer experiences, and member journeys that communicate CMC's value and impact.

Institutional Partnership Management
Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with foundations, corporations, and other community partners.
Manage foundation grant strategy, proposals, reports, and relationship development.
Cultivate existing corporate partnerships and renew lapsed partners that align with CMC's mission, membership community, and outdoor industry relationships.
Develop sponsorship, grant, and partnership strategies that support CMC programs, events, conservation initiatives, education, and organizational sustainability.
Maintain clear records of institutional deadlines, deliverables, reports, contacts, and relationship history.

Board, CEO & Leadership Partnership
Serve as the primary staff partner to the CEO on fundraising strategy, donor priorities, and development planning.
Support the Board of Directors and Development Committee with donor engagement strategy, fundraising materials, reports, and meeting preparation.
Prepare leadership briefings, donor profiles, solicitation plans, stewardship updates, and campaign materials as needed.
Help build shared accountability for philanthropy across board, staff, volunteers, members, and community partners.

Success in This Role Will Include

Within the first 12-24 months, the Development Director will:
Establish a clear development strategy and operating rhythm.
Improve donor data quality, reporting, and fundraising processes.
Increase engagement and retention among current donors and members.
Build a stronger pipeline of individual and institutional supporters.
Develop stronger relationships with key donors and prospects.
Create a sustainable foundation for future major giving, planned giving, and campaign readiness.

Experience & Qualifications

The ideal candidate will be a relationship-focused fundraising professional who combines strategic thinking with the ability to execute. They will enjoy simultaneously building systems, engaging people, and creating meaningful connections between individuals and CMC's mission.
CMC recognizes that strong candidates may bring different combinations of experiences and skills. If you are excited about this opportunity and believe you can contribute to our mission, we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every qualification outlined below. We value diverse career paths and experiences, transferable skills, and a willingness to learn and grow.

Required
5+ years of nonprofit fundraising experience with demonstrated success in individual giving, institutional giving, or relationship-based fundraising.
Experience managing donor relationships, pipeline strategies, and fundraising campaigns.
Proven ability to work collaboratively across teams, as well as with volunteer leadership.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Experience using fundraising databases and CRM systems.
Ability to work independently, prioritize multiple initiatives, and build effective partnerships.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Successful completion of a criminal background check.

Preferred
Experience with Salesforce.
Experience with major gifts, planned giving, or campaign preparation.
Experience working with membership-based organizations or community-driven nonprofits.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
Passion for outdoor recreation, conservation, and connecting people to the mountains.

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

Work is primarily office-based in Golden, Colorado, with hybrid flexibility available.
Regular in-person collaboration, donor meetings, board or committee meetings, and community engagement activities are expected.
Occasional evenings, weekends, outdoor programs, member events, donor events, and community events are required.
The position requires frequent computer work, donor and partner communications, meetings, presentations, and occasional local travel for cultivation or community engagement.

Compensation

CMC will offer the successful candidate a competitive compensation and benefits package comparable to nonprofit organizations of similar size and scope.
Salary Range: $75,000-$90,000 annually. Benefits include:
Health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance.
Generous vacation and sick leave.
Employer-matched retirement plan.
Discounts on outdoor gear and CMC technical schools.

Application Process

This search is being managed by the South Franklin Advisory Group. Please submit a resume and cover letter to southfranklinadvisory@gmail.com
, and include "CMC Development Director - First Name Last Name"
in the subject line.
Top candidates will be contacted for interviews or additional candidate screening. No phone calls please.

One Family’s mission is to prevent homelessness and break the cycle of family poverty in Massachusetts by promoting pathways to economic independence. Founded in 2000 in response to the growing crisis of family homelessness, One Family believes that education and career success are the foundations of lasting housing stability. This work is especially urgent in Massachusetts, where residents face some of the highest living costs in the country. Through two direct-service programs, the organization helps families at risk of or experiencing homelessness overcome barriers to higher education and family-sustaining careers, supporting their path toward lasting economic and housing stability. One Family pairs this work with public policy advocacy, engaging program participants on its Advocacy Team to use their lived experience to drive systemic change. Learn more about One Family’s programming and impact in 2025 here.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a rare opportunity to lead philanthropy at an organization with a strong, established funding base and a proven model of impact. Building on this solid foundation, One Family is seeking a strategic leader with a demonstrated ability to bring in new revenue and drive significant growth. As a key member of the executive team, the Senior Director of Development will help set organization-wide strategy alongside senior leadership, build and execute a bold revenue strategy, expand One Family's funding base, elevate its brand, and deepen donor relationships, at a pivotal moment in the organization's growth.

One Family enters this moment from a position of strength: a $2.7 million budget for FY2027, anchored by a solid base of philanthropic support and a $1.7 million philanthropic revenue target. You will have the resources, stability, and leadership support to build on this foundation—pursuing new funding streams, building strategic partnerships, and leading a talented three-person team.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Develop and execute a multi-year philanthropic growth strategy spanning corporate, foundation, and individual giving
Use fundraising data, pipeline analysis, and historical performance to actively manage revenue: setting realistic targets, prioritizing opportunities, allocating resources, and course-correcting when performance is off track
Develop strategies to engage and acquire new donors and funders across individual, corporate, and foundation giving

SoulBeing is a B2B healthcare platform, working through employers, brokers, channel partners, and strategic healthcare support organizations to bring these services to employees at scale. As the company enters its next stage of growth, they are seeking an exceptional executive leader to help scale the business and accelerate revenue growth.

Position Overview

The Chief Operating Officer / Chief Revenue Officer will serve as the CEO's primary strategic and operational partner, leading execution across revenue generation, operations, partnerships, and organizational growth.

This role requires an executive who can simultaneously think strategically and execute tactically. The ideal candidate is an accomplished revenue leader with experience in channel sales and partnership development, combined with the operational discipline required to build scalable systems and processes within a high-growth startup environment.

Develop performance metrics, KPIs, dashboards, and reporting systems.
Improve organizational efficiency and cross-functional coordination.
Build scalable infrastructure that prepares the organization for future growth and investment.

Executive Leadership

Drive accountability and execution across the organization.
Collaborate with leadership, investors, board members, and key stakeholders.
Help shape company strategy and organizational priorities.
Foster a culture of excellence, transparency, accountability, and mission alignment.

Expand broker and channel partnerships.
Successfully launch and grow strategic partnership initiatives.
Implement operational systems and processes that support scale.

Experience leading cross-functional teams and company-wide initiatives.
Strong operational and organizational management capabilities.

Experience working with benefit brokers, consultants, or employer-sponsored benefits programs.

Nice to Have

Healthcare, benefits, wellness, or digital health industry experience.
Experience with strategic platform partnerships and enterprise channel development.
Familiarity with HSA, FSA, HRA, or employee benefits ecosystems.

What Success Looks Like

You are a leader who:
Thrives in ambiguity and startup environments.
Combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
Builds trust quickly with customers, partners, investors, and team members.
Generates revenue while creating scalable operational infrastructure.
Inspires others through optimism, resilience, and accountability.
Believes deeply in expanding access to preventive, holistic, and evidence-based healthcare.

Why Join SoulBeing?

This is an opportunity to join an emerging healthcare technology company at a pivotal stage of growth. You will help shape the future of the organization, work directly alongside the founder, influence company strategy, and participate meaningfully in the value creation of the business through executive-level equity ownership.

Compensation includes a competitive base salary starting at $100,000 annually, performance-based incentives tied to company growth and results, and meaningful equity participation that aligns your success with the long-term success of the organization.

Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, and expertise, as evaluated during the interview process. jobs.description:
Confidential Music Licensing & Content Technology Company

The Opportunity

A profitable, founder-led music licensing and content technology company is seeking a driven Chief Executive Officer to lead its next stage of growth and position the business for financing or a strategic transaction.
Operating at the intersection of premium content, intellectual property, licensing, and technology, the company serves customers across digital media, entertainment, brands, agencies, and emerging content platforms. Its respected catalog, established relationships, and recurring and transactional revenue provide a strong foundation for expansion.
The incoming CEO will inherit a stable, profitable company with a talented, lean team and strong industry reputation, work closely with a seasoned co-founder during the transition, and build measurable enterprise value.

The Role

The CEO will own strategy, commercial performance, operations, talent, and long-term value creation.
The immediate priority is growth. In this hands-on role leading a 10-person company, the CEO must be equally comfortable in board discussions and personally advancing enterprise sales, partnerships, and key accounts.
During a thoughtful transition, the CEO will absorb institutional knowledge and transfer founder-held customer, creator, partner, and industry relationships into the organization.
The CEO will build scalable commercial capabilities, evaluate new products and markets, and prepare the company for strategic opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

Revenue Growth and Commercial Leadership

     Own the company’s revenue strategy and deliver sustainable, profitable growth.
     Personally lead enterprise sales, business development, and strategic partnership activity.
     Build and manage a disciplined sales pipeline, including clear targets, forecasting, conversion metrics, and accountability.
     Expand key accounts and partnerships across media, entertainment, technology platforms, agencies, brands, gaming, and adjacent markets.
     Develop new channels, licensing models, customer segments, and recurring-revenue opportunities while strengthening retention.
     Represent the company with senior executives, investors, partners, and potential strategic buyers.

Strategy and Enterprise Value Creation

     Develop and execute a focused growth plan, concentrating resources where the company has the greatest advantage.
     Evaluate organic growth, partnerships, acquisitions, financing, and other strategic alternatives.
     Improve revenue quality and predictability while protecting profitability.
     Establish the financial, commercial, operational, and governance discipline required for due diligence and a potential investment, merger, acquisition, or sale.
     Position the company for an attractive outcome without sacrificing current performance or long-term optionality.

Leadership and Operations

     Lead, motivate, and develop a small, experienced, multidisciplinary team.
     Translate strategy into clear priorities, goals, accountability, and operating rhythms.
     Allocate resources thoughtfully and add capabilities selectively as the business grows.
     Maintain a culture that values creativity, accountability, collaboration, responsiveness, and integrity.
     Align technology, rights, content, and service capabilities with commercial priorities.

Founder and Relationship Transition

     Partner with the co-founder to absorb institutional knowledge and understand key decisions and relationships.
    Build trust with long-standing customers, content partners, creators, and industry stakeholders while deliberately transferring founder-held relationships.
     Preserve the company’s reputation, culture, and relationship-centered approach while communicating the transition clearly and introducing changes required for growth.

Board and Financial Leadership

    Maintain a transparent, productive board relationship and report clearly on revenue, pipeline, profitability, cash, risks, and priorities.
     Own budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation, metrics, and overall business performance.

Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will be a commercially accomplished executive ready to assume full leadership of an entrepreneurial company.
They may be:
     An experienced growth-stage leader;
     A president, general manager, commercial or revenue leader ready to become CEO; or
     A founder or entrepreneurial business leader with relevant commercial and leadership experience.

Music-industry experience is highly desirable but not required. Relevant backgrounds include media, entertainment, content licensing, creator platforms, gaming, advertising technology, digital marketplaces, intellectual property, and adjacent technology-enabled businesses.

Required Experience and Capabilities

     A strong record in sales, business development, revenue leadership, or strategic partnerships.
     Executive leadership experience with responsibility for business performance, strategic execution, cross-functional relationships, and board engagement.
     Resourcefulness and a genuine interest in leading a lean organization through personal contribution and influence.
     Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.

Highly Valued Experience

     Music licensing, publishing, synchronization, production music, rights management, or music technology;
     Content licensing, intellectual property, digital media, gaming, creator platforms, or embedded media services;
     Subscription, SaaS, API, marketplace, or other technology-enabled business models;
     Scaling a company toward financing or a strategic transaction, including due diligence;
     Founder succession and building scalable commercial capabilities in a relationship-led organization.

     Commercially driven and energized by winning business;

     Motivated by building long-term enterprise value;
     Strategic and willing to work directly in the business;
     Curious about evolving media, technology, licensing, and content-consumption models;
     Respectful of creators, intellectual property, and long-standing partnerships; and
     Confident, decisive, accountable, transparent, and able to balance continuity with change.

The Director develops and implements the School’s communications, marketing, and advancement strategies while actively writing communications, creating campaigns and content, strengthening the School’s brand and visibility, and supporting fundraising and donor engagement.

Working closely with the Head of Administration, Head of School, and Director of Enrollment Management & Alumni Relations, the Director ensures that communications and advancement efforts support the School’s strategic priorities, strengthen community engagement, and contribute directly to family recruitment and retention and long-term sustainability.

The Director supervises the Marketing & Design Coordinator and leads the School’s communications and advancement functions. Communications & Digital Strategy

Create, write, edit, and publish internal and external communications, including newsletters, publications, website content, press releases, executive communications, and crisis communications.

Create and manage content across digital and print platforms, including photography, videography, publications, advertising, presentations, brochures, and other marketing materials.
Actively capture, write, edit, and publish authentic stories that showcase students, faculty, programs, and community life.
Maintain the school's photography, video, and digital asset library for ongoing marketing and communication needs.
Plan and execute major branding initiatives, website enhancements, anniversary campaigns, and other strategic communication projects.

Work collaboratively with faculty, staff, administrators, volunteers, and external vendors to deliver high-quality communication, marketing, and advancement initiatives.

Bachelor's degree in Communications, Marketing or a related field.

Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills with the ability to create engaging communications for diverse audiences.
Experience managing digital communications, websites, newsletters, social media, and marketing campaigns.
Experience managing multiple strategic projects simultaneously while maintaining exceptional attention to detail.
Strong relationship-building, organizational, and project management skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with external partners.
Professional working proficiency in both English and German, with excellent written and verbal communication skills in both languages.

Strong technology skills, including experience with content management systems, email communication platforms, design software, and digital collaboration tools.

Experience in an independent school or nonprofit organization.
Experience with fundraising, donor stewardship, sponsorships, or institutional advancement.
Experience implementing communication platforms (such as ParentSquare), CRM systems, or other communication technologies.
Photography, videography, or graphic design experience.
Experience working with international or bilingual communities.

The organization offers a mission-driven work environment focused on equity, inclusion, and sustainable community development.

Based in Shelburne, Vermont, Community Heart & Soul is seeking a Chief Operating Officer (COO) to serve as the organization's senior internal operating executive. Reporting directly to
the President, the COO leads day-to-day operations, staff coordination, financial management
support, and organizational infrastructure—enabling the President to remain fully focused on
national expansion, partnership development, and strategic growth.

statewide philanthropic networks, and civic organizations are key in the growth of Community
Heart & Soul's resident-led program. The COO will play a central role in ensuring that this
national growth is matched by strong systems, disciplined execution, and a thriving internal
culture—without veering into mission-creep. The COO upholds the organization's commitment
to its core identity as it scales.

partners, Heart & Soul communities, and attend conferences and events. 

1. Organizational Operations The COO ensures that Community Heart & Soul runs smoothly, efficiently, and professionally every day. • Oversee day-to-day operations and translate approved strategic priorities into clear, actionable work plans. • Coordinate internal systems across all departments and monitor progress against projects and deadlines. • Identify opportunities to improve workflows, meeting rhythms, reporting systems, and decision-making processes. • Ensure staff have the tools, information, and support needed to do their best work. • Maintain operational momentum and continuity as the organization grows—especially when the President is traveling or externally engaged.

2. 3. 5. About Colorado Mountain Club

Colorado Mountain Club (CMC) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting adventure, recreation, conservation, and education in the outdoors. Founded in 1912, CMC provides access to year-round activities, events, and schools tailored to a wide range of outdoor enthusiasts, from novices to experts. With over 6,000 members, CMC facilitates more than 3,000 trips annually and offers 250+ courses, fostering a dynamic community of adventure seekers and conservationists.

Position Overview

Colorado Mountain Club is seeking a Development Director to lead the next phase of growth and evolution of our fundraising program. This position represents an opportunity to build the foundation for long-term philanthropic success by strengthening donor relationships, improving development systems, and creating a clear pathway for members and supporters to become increasingly engaged with CMC.
The Development Director will serve as the organization's fundraising leader, responsible for developing and executing strategies that increase annual giving, expand major donor relationships, strengthen institutional partnerships, and position CMC for future campaign and legacy giving opportunities. This role is not simply focused on hitting annual revenue targets. It is focused on building a stronger culture of engagement and philanthropy among the thousands of individuals who already connect with CMC through membership, recreation, education, volunteerism, and conservation.

The successful candidate will help transform CMC's development efforts from a transactional fundraising approach into a relationship-based advancement model, creating systems and strategies that move individuals along a lifelong journey from public audience, to CMC member, donor, loyal supporter, and major or legacy donor. The Development Director will report directly to the CEO, serve as a member of the senior leadership team, and work closely with the Board of Directors and Development Committee. Over time, this role may evolve into broader advancement leadership as CMC continues to align development, membership, communications, and community engagement efforts.

Key Competencies

Development Strategy & Fundraising Leadership

Build and manage a comprehensive fundraising program spanning individual annual giving, major gifts, planned giving, foundation support, corporate partnerships, and event engagement.
Establish clear fundraising systems, processes, and performance metrics to support sustainable growth.
Create strategies to increase donor retention, second gifts, recurring giving, and long-term donor loyalty.
Partner with the CEO, Board members, and staff leadership on donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies.

Development Operations & Infrastructure
Strengthen development systems, policies, and processes to support effective fundraising operations.
Manage and improve data quality, reporting, and relationship management practices within Salesforce and other development systems.
Establish consistent practices for gift tracking, donor communications, stewardship, and reporting.
Partner with finance and operations staff to ensure accurate gift processing, reporting, reconciliation, and accountability.
Create dashboards, reports, and internal tools that help leadership understand fundraising performance and donor pipeline progress.

Donor Engagement & Relationship Building
Build authentic relationships with members, volunteers, donors, foundation program officers, corporate partners, and community supporters.
Manage a donor pipeline through research, identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Create meaningful engagement opportunities including donor cultivation events, outdoor experiences, stewardship activities, and personalized outreach.
Serve as a visible ambassador for CMC within Colorado's outdoor community and philanthropic landscape.
Develop personalized donor strategies that strengthen connection to CMC's mission, programs, conservation work, education, and community impact.

Community Engagement & Organizational Collaboration
Work collaboratively with membership and communications staff to create a unified approach to member engagement and donor development.
Help build an integrated community engagement strategy that strengthens the connection between participation, belonging, and philanthropy.
Collaborate on communications, campaigns, events, and storytelling that demonstrate CMC's impact and inspire support.
Support the continued evolution toward an integrated Community Engagement and Advancement model.
Partner across departments to identify donor stories, program outcomes, volunteer experiences, and member journeys that communicate CMC's value and impact.

Institutional Partnership Management
Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with foundations, corporations, and other community partners.
Manage foundation grant strategy, proposals, reports, and relationship development.
Cultivate existing corporate partnerships and renew lapsed partners that align with CMC's mission, membership community, and outdoor industry relationships.
Develop sponsorship, grant, and partnership strategies that support CMC programs, events, conservation initiatives, education, and organizational sustainability.
Maintain clear records of institutional deadlines, deliverables, reports, contacts, and relationship history.

Serve as the primary staff partner to the CEO on fundraising strategy, donor priorities, and development planning.
Support the Board of Directors and Development Committee with donor engagement strategy, fundraising materials, reports, and meeting preparation.
Prepare leadership briefings, donor profiles, solicitation plans, stewardship updates, and campaign materials as needed.
Help build shared accountability for philanthropy across board, staff, volunteers, members, and community partners.

Success in This Role Will Include

Within the first 12-24 months, the Development Director will:
Establish a clear development strategy and operating rhythm.
Improve donor data quality, reporting, and fundraising processes.
Increase engagement and retention among current donors and members.
Build a stronger pipeline of individual and institutional supporters.
Develop stronger relationships with key donors and prospects.
Create a sustainable foundation for future major giving, planned giving, and campaign readiness.

Experience & Qualifications

The ideal candidate will be a relationship-focused fundraising professional who combines strategic thinking with the ability to execute. They will enjoy simultaneously building systems, engaging people, and creating meaningful connections between individuals and CMC's mission.
CMC recognizes that strong candidates may bring different combinations of experiences and skills. If you are excited about this opportunity and believe you can contribute to our mission, we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every qualification outlined below. Occasional evenings, weekends, outdoor programs, member events, donor events, and community events are required.

One Family’s mission is to prevent homelessness and break the cycle of family poverty in Massachusetts by promoting pathways to economic independence. Founded in 2000 in response to the growing crisis of family homelessness, One Family believes that education and career success are the foundations of lasting housing stability. This work is especially urgent in Massachusetts, where residents face some of the highest living costs in the country. Through two direct-service programs, the organization helps families at risk of or experiencing homelessness overcome barriers to higher education and family-sustaining careers, supporting their path toward lasting economic and housing stability. Plan and execute major branding initiatives, website enhancements, anniversary campaigns, and other strategic communication projects.

Description:

C-Shift Consulting partners with leading organizations to solve complex business, organizational, and people challenges. We are looking for an experienced Director of Strategic Partnerships who brings together senior-level consulting expertise, relationship development, and business growth.
At its core, the Director of Strategic Partnerships is a builder of relationships - both with Clients and Consultants. This is someone who thrives by helping clients identify and articulate their needs, then aligning those needs with C-Shift's expertise, offerings, and people to create the right solution.

Just as important is supporting the success of our Consultants by matching the right skills to the work and the right personalities with the culture. This is a relationship-forward business development role focused on growing C-Shift’s impact across both new and existing clients- while ensuring the work we develop, is work we can deliver exceptionally well.

The right person reaps energy both from the business development process and the long-lasting account management relationship that follows. They enjoy uncovering opportunities, shaping solutions, and winning great work, but they are equally invested in what happens after the work is won. They may help stand up a new project, work directly on an engagement, advise Clients and Consultants, or continue developing the relationship as new needs emerge.

This is a role for someone who genuinely enjoys helping people solve problems, builds trust naturally, and has enough of a competitive streak to find satisfaction in turning strong relationships and great solutions into growth.

Role Overview:

This is a dual-track role: roughly 50% of your time will be spent as a billable senior consultant on client projects, with the other 50% focused on building relationships, developing business, and growing C-Shift's impact.

You'll work alongside our CEO and consulting team to identify client needs, shape solutions, develop new opportunities, and grow relationships over time. Depending on the engagement, you'll also help stand up new projects, facilitate senior leadership sessions, advise project teams, or work directly alongside clients as a senior consultant.

Core Responsibilities:
